title: Token Inspector — interactive prototype notes and backlog
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the interactive prototype notes for the Token Inspector — a console module that lets engineers drill into per-request and aggregated token-level cost and latency signals. Focus is on an exploratory experience (slice + dice) rather than a single static chart. Goals here are to converge on interactions, required derived metrics, and a prioritized grooming list for the next two sprints.

Goals and success metrics:
- Primary goal: Enable root-cause and unit-econ analysis at token granularity for production traffic. Users should answer: which model components, token positions, or routing decisions are driving cost or tail latency?
- Success metrics: time-to-insight for an incident (target: <12 min for a power user), number of regressions triaged using Token Inspector (tracking via CONSOLE tags), reduction in average per-token cost variance for top customers (quarterly).

Personas and core workflows:
- Platform Engineer (PE): Investigates a latency SLA breach. Wants per-route waterfall, request replay traces, and ability to filter by model variant and region.
- ML Engineer: Validates cost impact of quantization/kv-cache changes. Wants aggregate per-token cost by model and by quantization profile, plus sample request comparisons.
- Product Manager/Eng PM: Monitors unit-econ trends for a new conversational feature. Wants aggregated charts, cohort comparisons, and exportable summaries for stakeholders.

User stories (prioritized):
1) PE: "As a PE I can select a time window and see a waterfall of median/95/99 latency components (network, scheduling, model forward, postprocess) at token-level so I can find the dominant contributor."
2) ML Eng: "As an ML Eng I can compare two model variants side-by-side on per-token cost heatmaps and export sample prompt diffs."
3) PM: "As a PM I can define a cohort (route + model + region) and get a one-click cost snapshot and CSV export for finance."
4) SRE: "I can pin a request trace to persist for a follow-up investigation and annotate it."

Wireframe variants (notes + tradeoffs):
A. Compact Sparklane view (default): single-row per-route with small sparklines for cost and latency and an expander to open detailed view. Pros: high density, good for overview. Cons: less friendly for deep inspection. Best used as landing page.
B. Dual-pane Explorer (recommended for prototype): left pane: cohort/filters + timeline; right pane top: waterfall + sparkline; right pane bottom: sample request list and token heatmap. Pros: fast pivoting; Cons: more screen real-estate.
C. Modal deep-dive: open a single request in a modal that shows token-by-token timing, KV-cache hits, logits entropy, and cost attribution. Pros: focused; Cons: interrupts flow if used too often.

Detailed interaction patterns (hover / click semantics):
- Hover a token in the heatmap: show micropopover with token text (ellipsized), position index, forward-time ms, KV-hit boolean, incremental cost estimate, and links to the raw request id.
- Click a token: pin token and auto-scroll waterfall to the corresponding compute phase; timeline filters to similar token positions across cohort.
- Multi-select tokens in heatmap: aggregate metrics (sum cost, avg latency) for selected positions.
- Timeline brushing: updates both aggregated series and sample list.

Derived metrics to compute server-side (minimal viable set):
- per_token_cost_usd (estimated using token weight * model price profile)
- per_token_forward_ms (time in model forward for token position)
- kv_cache_hit_rate_by_position
- scheduling_wait_ms
- network_ms
- token_entropy (logits entropy approximation)
Notes: per_token_cost_usd will need to be a mapping from model variant -> price per 1K tokens; cache-aware discounts should be applied.

Microcopy and labels (to avoid confusion):
- "Incremental cost" — label for per-token marginal cost (vs. "cumulative cost").
- "Token heatmap" — subtitle: "cost & latency by position in response".
- CTAs: "Pin trace", "Export CSV", "Compare variant".

Accessibility notes:
- Heatmap must have an ARIA table fallback for keyboard navigation and screen readers, show summarized numeric tooltip for selected cell.
- Color scale should be perceptually uniform and have a high-contrast alternative toggle.

Backlog (rough priority ordering) — grooming-ready tickets:
- CONSOLE-842: Implement dual-pane layout scaffold + basic filters (time, route, model, region) [P0]
- CONSOLE-853: Server-side per-token cost / latency aggregation endpoints (rollup by cohort) [P0]
- CONSOLE-859: Token heatmap component + hover popover with micro-metrics [P1]
- CONSOLE-872: Waterfall component with mapped token anchors + request pinning [P1]
- CONSOLE-888: Export CSV / snapshot API and finance-friendly summary card [P2]
- CONSOLE-901: Modal deep-dive with KV-cache visualization and logits entropy [P2]
- CONSOLE-919: UX telemetry hooks (time-to-insight, feature usage) [P3]
Each ticket above should include acceptance criteria: data fields expected from backend, target perf (render <200ms for default cohort), and example cassettes (sample request ids).

Open questions / risks:
- Data volume: per_token traces are heavy — decide retention policy and sampled vs full ingestion. Proposal: full ingest for pinned/failed requests; 1% sampling for normal traffic with deterministic sampling for top customers.
- Cost model accuracy: we need a standard mapping for quantized vs fp16 vs int8 effective token cost; finance must sign off on approximation method.
- Privacy: ensure request-level identifiers are masked for PII-sensitive customers; make trace export opt-in per-customer.

Telemetry and observability for the feature:
- Events to emit: token_inspector_open, cohort_filter_apply, token_pin, export_snapshot. Capture duration of inspect session for UX analytics.

Prototype next steps (this sprint):
1) Design: deliver Figma dual-pane screens with annotated interactions (Nina) — due: +5 days.
2) Backend: wire up per-token cohort endpoint with synthetic sample (Ethan) — due: +10 days.
3) Frontend: stub dual-pane layout, heatmap placeholder, sample CSV export (Samir) — due: +12 days.
4) Grooming: break CONSOLE-842/853 into sub-tasks and assign owners — sprint planning.

Appendix: quick scenario walkthrough (for usability testing) — script for 10-min moderated test:
- Show landing list, ask tester to find cause of increased 95th latency in route "chat-completion-1" between 10–11am yesterday.
- Expected flow: filter to route -> open timeline -> spot spike -> open waterfall -> click sample -> hover token heatmap -> pin request -> export snapshot.
Success if tester completes in <12 minutes with no help.

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally interaction-heavy — we want to validate that a dual-pane approach supports both exploration and quick triage. Please add concrete design alternatives in Figma rather than long-form comments here.

End of doc.
